headline: Japan in 7 months, a real credit history by next fall

matches.explanation: Japan is your top goal, so it gets its own savings account. Separating the trip money keeps it from getting spent, and you can open it online for $50.
termsToKnow: $50 minimum to open online ($0 in branch)
$5 monthly fee, waived with a $500 average daily balance
6 transfers or withdrawals a month; $15 for each one over

matches.explanation: Your credit range is still building, and a secured card is the most reliable way to start. Two months of your credit allocation covers the $500 deposit without touching your trip fund.
termsToKnow: Credit limit equals your savings deposit, $500 to $2,000
APR not published; check current rate with FNB

matches.explanation: Everyday banking comes first. Student Checking has no monthly fee and no overdraft fees, and it's where you'll pay your card from each month so payments are always on time.
termsToKnow: No monthly service charge or minimum balance
No overdraft fees; transactions are declined when funds are short
Refunds non-FNB ATM fees up to 4 times per statement cycle

matches.unlockCondition: After Japan, once 3 months of expenses ($4,950) are saved
matches.explanation: A 12-month goal CD is a good home for your next big adventure fund. It's held back for now because its term runs past your 9-month trip.
termsToKnow: $100 minimum to open, plus at least $25 a month in transfers

steps.title: Open FirstRate Savings for your Japan fund
steps.detail: Name it "Japan" so the money has a job.

steps.title: Auto-save $469 a month for Japan
steps.detail: Schedule the transfer for payday. At this pace you reach $3,000 in about 7 months, ahead of your 9-month goal.

steps.title: Open Student Checking for everyday spending
steps.detail: No monthly fee and no overdraft fees while you're in school.

steps.title: Set aside $281 a month for your card deposit
steps.detail: Two months gets you to the $500 deposit for a secured card.

steps.title: Open a SmartSecured card with a $500 deposit
steps.detail: Use it for one small recurring bill, like your phone.

steps.title: Pay the full statement balance every month
steps.detail: On-time, paid-in-full payments are what build your score.

steps.title: After Japan, start a goal CD for your next adventure
steps.detail: Once your 3-month cushion is in place, a 12-month CD keeps long-range savings out of reach.

steps.title: Review your credit progress with an FNB banker
steps.detail: After a year of on-time payments, ask what your options look like.

notYet.reason: A 12-month CD would lock your Japan money past your 9-month trip, and early withdrawal has a penalty.
Not an unsecured credit card yet. With a building credit range, a secured card starts your history without likely denials or a high limit.
notYet.revisitWhen: after 6 to 12 months of on-time payments

bankerSummary: Maya, college student, not yet an FNB customer. Goals: study abroad in Japan ($3,000 in 9 months, priority 1) and build credit (12 months). Take-home $2,400/mo, fixed costs $1,500, debt payments $150, surplus $750/mo, savings $1,200, credit range: building. Plan: FirstRate Savings + Student Checking now, SmartSecured card in month 2, Savers Goal CD after the trip. Good fit for a student banking conversation.
disclaimer: Educational prototype. Not financial advice. No data is stored.
